subject: A/B testing beta enablement: SRE guardrails + runbook requirements
body:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: A/B testing beta enablement: SRE guardrails + runbook requirements

Dylan / Marissa,

Ahead of flipping the beta flag for route-level A/B testing, SRE needs a minimum set of guardrails + operational hooks in place. The feature is a traffic-shifting primitive, so we need fast detection and a deterministic rollback path when a variant regresses.

Below is what we’re asking to be “beta-ready” (not GA-ready):

1) Guardrail metrics (required in v1)
- Latency (by experiment_id + variant):
  - p95 end-to-end latency (request start -> final token / response end)
  - p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming routes
  - p99 end-to-end latency (for tail regressions)
- Reliability (by experiment_id + variant):
  - 5xx rate
  - 429 rate (explicitly; we saw this bite us in other rollouts)
  - timeout rate (gateway + upstream)
- Exposure sanity:
  - exposure_count per variant
  - allocation_drift (actual vs configured split) so we catch bucketing bugs quickly

2) Proposed beta guardrail thresholds (initial defaults)
These are intended as safe, not perfect. We can tune after dogfood/beta.

Rollback-triggering alerts (page) if sustained for >= 10 min AND >= 500 exposures in window:
- p95 end-to-end latency regression: > +15% relative vs control OR > +75ms absolute (whichever triggers first)
- p95 TTFT regression: > +20% relative vs control OR > +100ms absolute
- 5xx rate: > 0.5% absolute OR > 2x control (if control <0.25%)
- timeout rate: > 0.2% absolute
- 429 rate: > 0.3% absolute OR > 2x control

Non-paging (ticket / Slack) if sustained for >= 15 min:
- allocation drift: > +/- 3 percentage points from configured split after 10k exposures
- p99 latency regression: > +25% relative vs control

Notes:
- Using a minimum exposure count is important to avoid flapping on low volume.
- “Control” is defined as the designated baseline variant in the experiment config.

3) Required rollback / disable mechanisms
- A one-click “Stop experiment” action in Console must:
  - set routing to 100% control immediately (or nearest equivalent) and
  - emit an audit event (who/when/why)
- An emergency kill switch (config/feature-flag level) that SRE can toggle to disable ALL experiments in a region/tier if needed.
- A guardrail evaluator hook that can trigger an automatic rollback to control (even if the UI is down).

4) Runbook requirements (must exist before beta)
We need a single canonical runbook that covers:
- how to identify which experiment is responsible (experiment_id -> route/project)
- how to stop a specific experiment
- how to use the global emergency disable
- how to verify rollback (metrics to check, expected recovery timeline)
- comms template for Support/CS (what to say, where to log incident notes)

5) Alert routing / ownership (proposal)
- SRE owns the alert rules + paging integration.
- Console/Platform engineering owns:
  - implementing the rollback hook,
  - ensuring the stop/disable actions are reliable,
  - keeping the runbook steps accurate.
- PM owns:
  - confirming default thresholds and
  - deciding whether customers can override thresholds per experiment (I’d prefer “no” for beta).

If you’re aligned, I suggest we treat this as a beta gate in ENG-2848 (feature flag rollout plan) and track guardrail instrumentation under ENG-2845.

Happy to jump on a 20 min review today.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: A/B testing beta enablement: SRE guardrails + runbook requirements

Thanks Sean.

This all makes sense. A couple quick questions:
1) For the regression comparisons, are you expecting the guardrail evaluator to compute “vs control” directly, or can we initially alert on absolute thresholds per variant and do relative comparisons in the dashboard?
2) For 429s: do you want it scoped only to the experiment route (preferred) or global service-level 429s with experiment tags as a dimension?

We have the Console stop action in progress; kill switch is easy to add to config service (region/tier scoped).

I’ll add a beta gating checklist item to ENG-2848 and link this email.

- Dylan


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 11:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: A/B testing beta enablement: SRE guardrails + runbook requirements

Answers inline:

> 1) For the regression comparisons, are you expecting the guardrail evaluator to compute “vs control” directly, or can we initially alert on absolute thresholds per variant and do relative comparisons in the dashboard?

For beta, we can start with absolute thresholds in the paging path IF they’re conservative (e.g., 5xx > 0.5%, timeout > 0.2%, 429 > 0.3%, etc.).

But we should still implement “vs control” comparison in the evaluator as soon as practical. Absolute-only tends to either miss regressions when baseline is low or page constantly when baseline is noisy.

> 2) For 429s: do you want it scoped only to the experiment route (preferred) or global service-level 429s with experiment tags as a dimension?

Preferred is scoped to the experiment route/project. Global 429s are useful context but not actionable for “which experiment did it.” If we can only do global initially, we need a clear drilldown to experiment_id/variant.

One more beta gate I forgot to mention: on stop/rollback we need confirmation that routing has converged (i.e., we’re not still serving the variant due to cache/prop delays). Even a simple “effective_at” + propagation window note in UI/runbook is fine.

Let’s review thresholds quickly in the next rollout sync; I’m okay with these as defaults.

- Sean
